text:
jordan: Ran a focused DeepSurge-16B bring-up across fp16 / int8 / int6 / int5 for prod-sim slices (N=250: long summarization, multi-step QA, short assistant). Key takeaway: int6 gives a strong latency/cost cut with small quality impact; int5 is close but shows repeatable compression on procedural tasks.

lee: can you drop the compact scorecard + deltas so we can hand it to GTN? numbers + short notes pls.

jordan: here's the mini-scorecard (avg across slices): ROUGE-L / BLEURT / p50 latency @ 1024 / est cost($/1k tokens)

jordan: ```
variant | ROUGE-L | BLEURT | p50 ms | cost($/1k)
fp16    | 0.778   | 0.90   | 150    | 1.00
int8    | 0.771   | 0.88   | 120    | 0.68
int6    | 0.766   | 0.875  | 100    | 0.56
int5    | 0.760   | 0.87   | 95     | 0.50

delta int6 vs fp16: -1.5% ROUGE-L, -2.7% BLEURT, -33% p50, -44% cost
delta int5 vs fp16: -2.3% ROUGE-L, -3.3% BLEURT, -37% p50, -50% cost
```

pat: good context. Where does int5 break vs int6? failure-mode breakdown?

jordan: triage for int5 regressions on long-context QA: ~58% loss of intermediate procedural steps, ~27% mild factual drifts (numerics/dates), ~15% occasional truncation/stop anomalies. Short turn chat unaffected for both int6/int5.

tara: tail latencies? 95/99p values?

jordan: 95p: fp16 430ms, int8 330ms, int6 280ms, int5 260ms. 99p: fp16 800ms, int6 560ms, int5 540ms. Lower precision tightens tails due to packing and lower memory pressure.

lee: product asks for a recommended routing policy and rollout gates for GTN.

jordan: recommended routing + gating: - Default: deepsurge-16b-int6 for consumer and API traffic. - Route to fp16 for requests with input_tokens > 700 OR tag: "high_precision" OR route: "financial/legal". - Reserve int5 for internal batch summarization and experimental workloads only.

jordan: rollout gates (proposed): - Allow int6 if ROUGE-L drop <= 2% absolute AND BLEURT delta <= 3% AND hallucination increase <= 2pp on holdout slices. - Block int5 from high-recall routes; int5 requires vendor kernel verification and 72h shadow + manual audit before any user-facing traffic.

jordan: sample routing snippet: ```json
{"routing": {"default_model": "deepsurge-16b-int6", "rules": [{"match": {"input_tokens_gt": 700}, "model": "deepsurge-16b-fp16"}, {"match": {"request_tag": "high_precision"}, "model": "deepsurge-16b-fp16"}]}}
```

pat: ops items? kernels, dedicated pools, canary percentages?

jordan: ops notes: int6 kernel already available on our fleets; int5 uses a vendor runtime that needs validation on dedicated nodes. Recommend canary: 4% traffic for int6 (shadow 100%), and for int5 start with 1% + full shadow and manual sample audit. Add auto-eval hook to fail rollout if hallucination > 3pp or ROUGE-L drop > 2% after 24h.

lee: econ sketch for GTN slide? what's the rough monthly impact if we flip most traffic to int6?

jordan: back-of-envelope: baseline all fp16 = $220k/month. With mix 75% int6, 20% int8, 5% fp16 => ~$153k/month (~30% savings). If we convert 10% of batch to int5 (experimental) incremental savings -> ~$145k/month. Plan budget with 10% reserve => ~$160k/month.

tara: will GTN accept those gates? I'll join the sync to present the failure samples and the risk controls.

deploy-bot: Canary created: canary/deepsurge-int6-2024-08-01 (traffic 4%). See /deploys/5522

lee: great. Jordan, please attach the focused holdout queries and a few annotated failure examples in the canary ticket. We'll reconvene after 24h metrics.

jordan: will do. filing follow-up once 24h data is in.
